target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken (e.g. the sandbox container is destroyed mid-flight), the Node stream layer emits `error` events on the child's stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts` and other sibling spawn paths: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

- The fix is a 3-line addition following the established `ignoreOutputStreamError` pattern used across `src/agents/`, `src/infra/`, and `src/auto-reply/`.
- `process.on("error", ...)` already covers spawn failures; the new listeners cover independent stream-level pipe failures.
- No existing tests mock `child_process` in this extension; the runtime behavior is exercised by existing sandbox integration tests.
